speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe your headache in detail; is it sudden and severe, or does it develop gradually? Have you noticed any specific visual disturbances like floaters, flashes of light, or a shadow in your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Is the headache located on one side of your head or does it affect both sides? Have you experienced any weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking alongside the visual changes? REQUEST TEST: MRI of the brain with contrast.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculous Meningitis. Given the patient's age, subacute headache, worsening vision, and specific suspicion of TB, immediate initiation of anti-tubercular therapy and intracranial pressure monitoring is critical. Please request the MRI results and a lumbar puncture to confirm the diagnosis.
